Salesforce Delivery

AI-Augmented Practice

• Use AI development tooling - Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot - as primary daily tooling, not as an optional aid.

• Pair with the AI Solutions Engineer on Salesforce-side agent integration and on exposing Salesforce data and actions to agents safely.

• Contribute reusable prompts and patterns to the shared prompt/pattern library, and provide feedback that improves COE agents.

• Participate in code reviews - both giving and receiving - with attention to the correctness of AI-generated work.

• Uphold PHI/HIPAA handling standards in all Salesforce and AI-assisted work.

MINIMUM KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

• 5+ years of Salesforce development experience, including Apex, LWC, and SOQL.

• Experience with Salesforce Health Cloud or a comparable Salesforce industry cloud.

• Experience building Salesforce integrations (REST APIs, Platform Events, external services).

• Demonstrated use of - or strong readiness to adopt - AI-assisted development tooling (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or Einstein for Developers).

• Sound understanding of prompt engineering for code generation and of how to review AI-generated code critically.

• Comfortable delivering in a fast-paced, compressed-timeline, parallel-track environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Salesforce Platform Developer I/II certification.

• Healthcare, life-sciences, or Patient Services domain experience.

• Exposure to AI agents, RAG, or LLM-based workflows in a development context.

• MuleSoft or DataWeave familiarity.

Tools & Stack

• AI development: Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Einstein for Developers.

• Salesforce: Salesforce Platform, Health Cloud, ACTICS.

• Integration: MuleSoft / DataWeave.

• Lifecycle: Git, Azure DevOps, JIRA.

First-Year Success Measures

• Consistent delivery of ACTICS roadmap features at the team's AI-accelerated velocity targets.

• AI development tooling used routinely, with measurable contribution to code-generation and test-automation metrics.

• COE-built agents successfully integrated into Salesforce workflows for at least the priority use cases.

We're hiring a Finance & Accounts professional to own day-to-day accounting, compliance, and financial operations for our India entity. This isn't a traditional bookkeeping role. You'll be expected to run a lean, largely self-operating finance function - using AI tools and automation to eliminate manual, repetitive work, and spending your own time on judgment calls, exceptions, and analysis instead.
We'd rather hire someone who can build a system that does 80% of the reconciliation for them than someone who reconciles quickly by hand.

What You'll Own

• Books & Compliance : Day-to-day bookkeeping, vendor and customer invoicing, GST/TDS filings, payroll compliance, and statutory filings (ROC, PF, PT, etc.) for the India entity.

• Reconciliations : Bank, vendor, and intercompany reconciliations - ideally with a system in place that flags exceptions rather than requiring line-by-line manual matching.

• Month-end close : Own the close calendar, journal entries, accruals, and reporting packages; work toward shrinking close time quarter over quarter.

• AP/AR operations : Invoice processing, payment runs, collections follow-up, and expense management.

• Audit & compliance readiness : Coordinate with auditors, tax consultants, and company secretary; maintain audit-ready documentation continuously rather than scrambling at year-end.

• Process automation : Identify manual, repetitive finance workflows and either configure existing tools or use AI/no-code automation to remove yourself from the loop.

What We're Looking For

Core finance skills

• 2-5 years of experience in accounting/finance operations, ideally at a startup or fast-growing company (SaaS experience is a strong plus).

• Strong working knowledge of Indian accounting standards, GST, TDS, and statutory compliance.

• Hands-on experience with an accounting system (Zoho Books, Tally, QuickBooks, or similar); ERP exposure (NetSuite) is a bonus.

• Comfortable owning the full close cycle independently, not just executing assigned tasks.

AI & automation fluency (this matters as much as the accounting knowledge)

• Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) fluently for drafting communications, summarizing policies, researching compliance questions, and building financial models or analyses.

• Use AI to accelerate reconciliation and variance analysis - e.g., feeding bank statements and ledgers into a tool to auto-match entries and surface only genuine exceptions for human review.

description:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Benchling is looking for a Revenue Manager to own key areas of our revenue accounting and Order to Cash functions in a high-growth SaaS environment. This is a hands-on individual contributor role built for someone who wants deep technical ownership: the deferred revenue process, the end-to-end allowance process, contract modification accounting, and the revenue implications of new AI-driven business models.

You will be a core contributor to the revenue close alongside the broader team, while carrying full ownership of your areas end to end. A significant part of this role is forward-looking: helping shape how Benchling recognizes revenue on consumption-based products and how we track and account for AI partnership economics as those models evolve.

- Lead or assist on special projects such as new product and pricing model launches, entity or geographic expansion.

- Owner for designated audit areas during the annual audit - managing PBC deliverables, resolving auditor inquiries, and driving issues to closure.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

- BS/BA in Accounting, strong GAAP/GL/financial statement command. CPA strongly preferred.

- 7+ years progressive revenue accounting experience in a SaaS/software company, with deep hands-on ASC 6

title: Applied AI Security Engineer
description:
Waabi , founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun, is the leader in Physical AI. With a world-class team, we're unlocking the next era of autonomous transportation with technology that's powering commercial autonomous trucks and robotaxis. Waabi is backed by and partners with world leaders in AI, automotive, logistics, and deep tech.
With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit:

Waabi is leaning into an AI-native strategy - not just in our trucks, but in how we build, ship, and operate every day. Our teams leverage key AI tools to enhance productivity and efficiency, continuously expanding AI integration across our systems and workflows. That's a huge unlock, and it's moving fast. We're looking for someone to make sure it keeps moving fast safely - by establishing the guardrails and collaborating on the implementation of sandboxes and automations that let people adopt AI with confidence instead of second-guessing themselves. You'll join a small, sharp security team and take primary ownership of AI security controls and considerations across the company. If you've got a developer's instincts, a security mindset, and you're genuinely curious about what these tools can and can't be trusted to do, this role is built around you.
You will...

• Audit how AI tools and MCP integrations are currently used across the company, and map where they touch sensitive systems, data, or credentials for the purpose of defining policy.

• Design and implement layered guardrails - enterprise-level system prompts, scoped permissions, sandboxing patterns - that constrain AI behavior before it ever reaches a user's request.

• Maintain an inventory of both MCP servers and AI-to-service connections and their data access controls, with a clear model of what each one can access and why.

• Partner directly with users across the organization to bake secure-by-default patterns into their AI-assisted workflows so that written policy doesn’t just sit on a shelf.

• Evaluate new AI tools, plugins, and integration requests, and figure out the secure way to say yes.

• Continuously test and red-team your own guardrails - assume they'll be pushed on, and find the gaps before someone else does.

• Document guidance and patterns that a non-security audience can actually follow without needing a security background.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.

• Professional software development experience, with solid fundamentals in how services, APIs, and permissions fit together.

• Hands-on experience using AI coding/productivity tools (Claude, Copilot, Gemini, or similar) in business-critical workflows.

• Working knowledge of core security concepts - least privilege, sandboxing, trust boundaries, threat modeling basics.

• Strong communication skills - you work with engineers as a partner.

Bonus:

• Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or similar tool-calling/agent-integration frameworks.

• Exposure to prompt injection, jailbreaking, or other AI/LLM-specific attack techniques.

• Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, or other safety-critical systems

Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building.

Agents are becoming the default way developers ship LLM-powered software, and they are miserable to debug. A single run fans out across model calls, tool calls, retries, handoffs between agents, and multi-turn conversations that only make sense as a whole. When one goes wrong, the developer usually has a log line and a shrug.

Sentry's Agent Tracing https://docs.sentry.io/product/agents/ turns that into something you can actually inspect: agent runs, tool calls, model interactions, token usage and cost, conversations you can replay message by message.

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Telemetry Experience team, you'll own that product surface - Python/Django and Postgres on the backend, React and TypeScript on the frontend, sitting on top of Sentry's trace storage. You'll work with the SDK engineers who instrument the agent frameworks upstream and own everything customers touch downstream: the dashboards, the conversation views, the APIs, and the workflows that turn a confusing agent run into an obvious fix.

IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

- Own projects end to end. Take a problem from a rough customer complaint through scoping, design, implementation across the stack, rollout, and measurement. You'll write the design doc, cut the work into shippable pieces, and stay with it until the numbers move.

- Build the views developers debug agents in. Multi-agent workflows, conversation replay, cost and token breakdowns, the moment where a run failed and why. Making a deeply nested, wildly variable trace legible is a genuinely hard interface problem.

- Make the data underneath fast and queryable. Filtering and sorting millions of conversations, getting cost calculation right, and designing APIs that both humans and other people's agents can use well.

- Detect the failures worth flagging. We're expanding from showing developers what happened to telling them what went wrong - common agent failure classes surfaced as issues, not as something you have to go looking for.

- Take the friction out of getting started. Setup should be trivial on any stack, whether a developer wires it up by hand or asks their coding agent to do it.

- Collaborate daily with product managers, designers, SDK engineers, and other product engineers. - You're obsessed with making an experience smooth. Friction offends you. You notice the extra click, the confusing label, the query that takes 400ms too long - and you fix them instead of filing them.

- You want to build in a space that's still being figured out. Nobody has settled what agent observability should look like. You'd rather help decide that than implement someone else's finished answer.
